texts.preamble: Sanjay Pathak vs The State Of M.P. on 16 October, 2020 Author: Anand Pathak Bench: Anand Pathak High Court Of Madhya Pradesh 1 M.Cr.C.No.33318/2020 (Sanjay Pathak Vs. State of M.P.)
texts.facts: With consent heard on the point on admission through Video Conferencing. The instant petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is being preferred for quashment of FIR registered vide No. 32/2020 dated 24/1/2020 at Police Station Purani Chhawani, District Gwalior for offence registered under Section 274 of IPC, Section 27 of Drugs and Cosmetic Act, 1940 and Section 13 of Drugs Control Act, 1950. Precisely stated facts of the case are that petitioner possess two licences, one licence under the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 bearing licence No. 11419570000049 on the registered address Kelax Health Care, Saint John Vinni School, Purani Chhawani and the second licence bearing No. 20B/195/57/2016, which is a licence to sell, stock or exhibit or offer for sale, or distribute by whole sale drugs other than specified in (Schedule C, C(1) and X) on the address Goverdhan Colony, Bhind Road, District Gwalior. It appears that on 24/1/2020 around 12.30 pm Drugs HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Sanjay Pathak Vs. State of M.P.) Inspector, Food and Drugs Department, State of Madhya Pradesh, District Gwalior (respondent No. 2) conducted a sudden inspection at the premises of present petitioner and found some packaging material, Machinery related to manufacturing of drugs, unlabelled bottles and adulterated drugs at the premises, therefore Drugs Inspector lodged the FIR against the present petitioner and other co-accused persons for offence referred above. Respondent No. 2 with the help of other authorities conducted this raid on petitioner's premises under his authority and arrested Manish Joshi and Rahul Dubey, who were present on the spot but another co-accused Udal Singh Bhadauriya, who was also present on the spot could not be arrested and apparently he fled away. It further appears that respondent No. 2 being the authority under the Drugs and Cosmetic Act, 1940 (for short "Act of 1940"), therefore, filed the complaint under the provisions of Section 18 (c) which is punishable under Section 27 (b) (ii) of Act of 1940 and since the offence is repeated Sanjay Pathak vs The State Of M.P. on 16 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116750914/ 1 therefore, it is punishable under Section 30 (1) (a) of Act of 1940 also. Therefore, in sum and substance, complaint filed by respondent No. 2 is for offence under Section 27 (b) (ii), 30 (1) (a) of the Act HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Sanjay Pathak Vs. State of M.P.) of 1940 and Section 13 of the Drugs Control Act, 1950 (for short " Act of 1950").
texts.arguments: It is the submission of learned senior counsel for the petitioner that alleged adulterated / expired drugs do not belong to petitioner. In fact it belongs to one Alok Mishra, who filed an application under Section 451 and 457 of Cr.P.C. to claim those drugs which were found in the premises of petitioner. According to Alok Mishra, drugs belonged to him and he sent those drugs in an auto rickshaw for placing those drugs in a pit in some remote area but auto which carried the drugs got some problem and therefore, as a stop gap arrangement, those expired drugs were kept in the premises of petitioner and therefore those drugs never belonged to the petitioner. Another ground raised by petitioner is regarding jurisdiction and competence as according to learned senior counsel, complaint can only be filed by Drugs Inspector under Section 190-200 of Cr.P.C. and not by police and here FIR has been registered at the instance of police officer and thereafter charge-sheet has been filed, therefore, same is without authority. In support of his submissions, he relied upon decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Union of India Vs. Ashok Kuamr HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Sanjay Pathak Vs. State of M.P.) Sharma and Ors. 2020 SCC Online SC 683. To augment his arguments, he also relied upon judgment rendered in the case of S.B.Ganguly alias Satya Brata Ganguly Vs. State of Bihar and Anr., 1998 SCC Online (PAT) 170. It is further submitted that Section 274 of IPC is a cognizable offence and except on complaint, cognizance cannot be taken. He referred the representation preferred by wife of petitioner to submit that false case has been prepared against her husband. Petitioner being innocent has been falsely implicated, therefore, his case be considered in light of submissions made above and petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. be allowed and case registered against the petitioner be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Per contra, learned Panel Lawyer appearing on behalf of respondents/State opposed the prayer and submits that as per notification dated 19/2/2008, respondent No. 2-Drugs Inspector has been notified as Inspector as per Section 21 of the Act of 1940 and he has authority to file complaint and in the instant case complaint has been filed, therefore, no legal impairment exists qua present case. Looking to the contents of complaint, sufficient case is made out for trial. Petitioner is still absconding, therefore, case has been filed in his absence and he is not cooperating in HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Sanjay Pathak Vs. State of M.P.) investigation as well as in trial. He prayed for dismissal of the petition. HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Sanjay Pathak Vs. State of M.P.) Seizure memo was prepared and all procedures in accordance with law were undertaken. In fact, a complaint has been filed by the Drugs Inspector against the accused persons and therefore, contention of learned senior counsel for the petitioner sans merits regarding authority and jurisdiction because respondent No. 2 was well within his authority to file complaint and any police officer (or Investigating Officer for that matter) has not filed the charge-sheet as tried to be projected by learned senior counsel for the petitioner. Apex Court in the case of H.N.Rishbud Vs. State of Delhi, AIR 1955 SC 196, has considered this aspect and held in para 9 as under:- "9.The question then requires to be considered whether and to what extent the trial which follows such investigation is vitiated. Now, trial follows cognizance and cognizance is preceded by investigation. But it HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Sanjay Pathak Vs. State of M.P.) does not necessarily follow that an invalid investigation nullifies the cognizance or trial based thereon. While no doubt, in one Sanjay Pathak vs The State Of M.P. on 16 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116750914/ 3 HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Sanjay Pathak Vs. State of M.P.) sense, clauses (a), (b) and (c) of Section 190 (1) are conditions requisite for taking of cognizance, it is not possible to say that cognizance on an invalid police report is prohibited and is therefore a nullity. To such a situation section 537 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which is in the following terms is attracted: "Subject to the provisions herein before contained, no finding, sentence or order passed by a Court of competent jurisdiction shall be reversed or altered on appeal or revision on account of any error, omission or irregularity in the complaint, summons, warrant, charge, proclamation, order, judgment or other proceedings before or during trial or in any enquiry or other proceedings under this Code, unless such error, omission or irregularity, has in fact occasioned a failure of justice". If, therefore, cognizance is in fact taken, on a police report vitiated by the breach of a mandatory provision relating to investigation, there can be no doubt that the result of the trial which follows it cannot be [LEAKAGE_MASK] unless the illegality in the HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Sanjay Pathak Vs. State of M.P.) investigation can be shown to have brought about a miscarriage of justice. That an illegality committed in the course of investigation does not affect the competence and the jurisdiction of the Court for trial is well settled as appears from the cases in Prabhu vs. Emperor, (1861) 30 LJ Ch 379 and Lumbhardar Zutshi Vs. The King, Criminal Appeals Nos 25-D and 434 of 1953 disposed of on 3rd May, 1954. These no doubt relate to the illegality of arrest in the course of investigation while we are concerned in the present cases with the illegality with reference to the machinery for the collection of the evidence. We are, therefore, clearly, also, of the opinion that where the cognizance of the case has in fact been taken and the case has proceeded to termination., the invalidity of the precedent investigation does not vitiate the result, unless miscarriage of justice has been caused thereby." Said judgment of Apex Court still holds the field and has been referred in judgment of Apex Court in the case of Vinubhai Haribhai Malviya andOrs. Vs. State of Gujrat and Anr.,2019 SCC Online SC 1346 and the judgment rendered in the case of HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Sanjay Pathak Vs. State of M.P.) Ashok Kukmar Sharma (supra) as relied upon by the petitioner. Conclusions drawn by Apex Court in the case of Ashok Kumar Sharma (supra) are reproduced for ready reference:- "162. In regard to cognizable offences under Chapter IV of the Act, in view of Section 32 of the Act and also the scheme of the Cr.P.C., the Police Officer cannot prosecute Sanjay Pathak vs The State Of M.P. on 16 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116750914/ 4 offenders in regard to such offences. VII. We further direct that the Drugs Inspectors, who carry out the arrest, must not only report the arrests, as provided in Section 58 of the CrPC, but also immediately report the arrests to their superior Officers." One surprising aspect in the case is that petitioner is still absconding for last almost nine months alongwith another co- accused Udal Singh Bhadauriya, who was although present on spot but later on fled away and after so many months, petitioner has; not only filed this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. but also anticipatory bail application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Sanjay Pathak Vs. State of M.P.) vide M.Cr.C.No. 34641/2020 that too apparently when this Court expressed surprise over the conduct of police officers while granting temporary bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. to other co- accused Manish Joshi and Rahul Dubey vide order dated 1/9/2020 in M.Cr.C. Nos. 16078/2020 and 14611/2020 respectively and asked the report of concerned Police Officer (SHO) about the steps taken in this regard.
